rationale.risk-routing: Model computes which agent steps trigger human supervision checkpoints.
rationale.hitl-workflow: Scheduled checkpoints let users verify, diagnose, correct, and block progression.
rationale.oversight-explanation: Clickable traces and screenshots support human diagnosis of agent errors.
rationale.automation-bias: Users overlooked errors expecting agents to correct themselves later.
rationale.survey-input: Reports substantive preferences and perceived burdens for confirmation strategies.
rationale.counterpoint: Challenges prevalent confirm-at-end autonomy and constant-review extremes.
rationale.framework: Reusable decision-theoretic scheduling layer integrates with existing control hooks.
rationale.built-system: Implemented scheduler in a functional web prototype and evaluated it.
rationale.general-ai: Targets general-purpose agents across shopping, editing, office, and gaming tasks.
rationale.non-developer: Studies ordinary users supervising agents on nonprogramming tasks.
rationale.agentic: Autonomous multi-step agents deliver task trajectories at checkpoint granularity.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Empirically examines missed errors, complacency, and trust-calibration safeguards.
rationale.method-self-report: Uses interviews, think-aloud reports, questionnaires, and preference surveys.
rationale.method-experiment: Controlled within-subjects study compares intermediate and end confirmation.
